clue.text: Final defeat of the Wife of Prague, say?

indicators.note: say asks the solver to hear the phrase spoken, not read it as written

parts.note: a Prague man's wife is his Czech mate

explanation.surface: A question about the last downfall of some legendary woman from Prague.
explanation.walkthrough: A Czech mate (the partner of a man from Prague) sounds just like the chess term.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the game ends when a king is trapped with no escape, the final defeat.

clue.text: Diogenes for one, liable to 23

definitions.meaning: Diogenes of Sinope was the famous philosopher of the school that scorned convention
23 is clue 23-down, to scoff or curl the lip in contempt

explanation.definitionFit: Diogenes belonged to the ancient school of philosophers who scorned convention, and a scornful person is prone to scoffing.

clue.text: Wearing fur, like Hamelin's dignitaries

definitions.meaning: dressed in the white winter fur of the stoat
in the Pied Piper poem the Mayor and Corporation of Hamelin wear robes trimmed with stoat fur

explanation.definitionFit: Robed in white stoat fur, as were the Mayor and Corporation in Browning's Pied Piper of Hamelin.

clue.text: His victim a sleeping child ?

parts.note: read as kid plus napper, a child who naps, the abductor's victim being a child

explanation.walkthrough: A kid napping is a sleeping child, so the abductor's name splits into a child and a dozer.
explanation.definitionFit: An abductor who seizes someone, often a child, for ransom.

clue.text: So agreement is obtained by lying perhaps

parts.note: accord means agreement

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters of the next word as one possible arrangement among others

explanation.surface: Consensus is reached through deceit, as it may be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges LYING to INGLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore or in consequence, the sense of so as a connective.

clue.text: Tiller topped with this wood

indicators.note: topped means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: a tiller steers a boat, as the helm does

explanation.surface: A boat's tiller crowned with a piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes the first letter of HELM.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous tree whose timber is a familiar hardwood.

clue.text: Policemen take note of this wooded area

parts.note: cops is slang for police officers
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Officers are told to keep a record of a patch of woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thicket of trees, a coppice, is a little wooded area.

clue.text: Goods found about Jason's ship

parts.note: about gives C
the Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: Merchandise discovered aboard the Argonauts' vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight, the goods carried by a ship.

clue.text: Butterfly setter of note

parts.note: the famous composer who set Madama Butterfly to music

explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests a collector who pins butterflies, but it is one who sets words to music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian composer who wrote the opera Madama Butterfly.

clue.text: Extended note written in troubled Donegal

indicators.note: written in puts one piece inside another, as words are written in a space
troubled means stirred up, so the county's letters are disordered

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A drawn-out note scrawled in an Irish county in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a written message, but it is the sol-fa note, slipped into the scrambled county name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthened or drawn out, as something stretched is extended.

clue.text: Roaming Dominica? Not I

indicators.note: roaming letters wander out of their order, so the island's name is rearranged after dropping a letter

explanation.surface: Someone declines an island-hopping trip round the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue lost its final 'I'. 'Roaming' signals rearranging DOMINICA once the I is set aside ('Not I'), and also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering people with no fixed home lead a roaming life.

clue.text: It may be binding in N.W. Africa

definitions.meaning: a fine goatskin leather used to bind books
the kingdom in the north-west corner of Africa

explanation.definitionFit: Fine goatskin leather named after the country is used for book bindings, and the country lies in north-west Africa.

clue.text: Mac is unable to identify this plant

definitions.meaning: a Scot (Mac) would say he cannot in Scots dialect
a tropical flowering plant with large leaves

explanation.definitionFit: Scots dialect for cannot, as a Scotsman might say, and also a lily-like tropical garden plant.

clue.text: Bill's judgment

definitions.meaning: a bill, as at an inn, is the tally of what is owed
an estimate or appraisal of a situation

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Bill's' as 'Bill is': the account presented at an inn is the old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An itemized account to be paid, and also a considered estimate or appraisal.

clue.text: String teacher Nell replaced

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A music teacher called Nell is sacked and someone else takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges TEACHER NELL.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest-pitched string of a violin or lute is named this.

clue.text: With which to fish for perch

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length, five and a half yards

explanation.definitionFit: An angler's pole, and also an old measure of length, the same as a pole or perch.

clue.text: Stay which may be desirable for the liver?

definitions.text: Stay which may be desirable for the liver?

parts.words: Stay which may be desirable for the liver
parts.note: an estate agent's desirable home, a liver being one who lives there

explanation.walkthrough: 'liver' looks like the organ, but means one who lives; estate agents advertise a 'desirable' home.
explanation.definitionFit: A home, where one stays, often advertised as desirable.

clue.text: Frank's contribution may he conspicuous in his collection

definitions.text: Frank's contribution may he conspicuous in his collection

parts.words: Frank's contribution may he conspicuous in his collection
parts.note: frank here is the postmark on a used stamp, prominent in an album of a stamp collector

explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a person's name, but a frank is a postal cancellation mark, so the collector is of postage stamps.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp collector's album holds used stamps that bear postmarks, or franks.

clue.text: Plant lies with weeds in the wild

indicators.note: in the wild suggests letters let loose and running free in a new order

explanation.surface: A flower growing among weeds out in untamed country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wild' rearranges LIES and WEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alpine flower with white woolly bracts.

clue.text: To vote for the right? She demonstrated the contrary

definitions.text: To vote for the right? She demonstrated the contrary

parts.words: To vote for the right? She demonstrated the contrary
parts.note: a campaigner who marched for women's right to vote, read as the opposite of voting for it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Conservative voter; the campaigner instead demonstrated for the right to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Early twentieth-century British women campaigners demonstrated for the right to vote.

clue.text: French leader is certain to find an opening

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A French head of state is confident of finding a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack or narrow split is an opening.

clue.text: Not one of the Gentlemen made the first century

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
the first century is counted from AD 1, Anno Domini

explanation.surface: A cricketer from outside the amateur ranks scored the opening hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: In English cricket Gentlemen were the amateurs who played the professional Players; a man who is no gentleman is a bounder.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who behaves dishonourably is the opposite of a gentleman.

clue.text: Caesar's third act, to do so

definitions.text: Caesar's third act, to do so

parts.words: Caesar's third act, to do so
parts.note: Caesar's I came, I saw, I overcame: the third deed in his boast

explanation.walkthrough: 'act' suggests a play's third act; it is the last deed of veni, vidi, vici.
explanation.definitionFit: Vici, the third word of Caesar's boast, means I overcame.

clue.text: Apollyon's warship

definitions.meaning: Apollyon, in the Book of Revelation, is the angel whose name means the one who destroys

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Apollyon's' as 'Apollyon is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollyon is the biblical name meaning one who lays waste, and a fast naval escort vessel bears that name.

clue.text: On such a day we spend our savings

definitions.text: On such a day we spend our savings

parts.words: On such a day we spend our savings
parts.note: people save up for a day of hardship, proverbially a wet one

explanation.definitionFit: Saving 'for a wet day' means putting money by for hard times.

clue.text: In which one waits for a pilot's badge?

definitions.meaning: actors wait offstage at the sides of the stage
the winged emblem awarded to a qualified airman

explanation.definitionFit: The offstage sides of a theatre where actors wait, and an airman's winged badge.

clue.text: Sheridan's lady could do so well as one of his critics

definitions.text: Sheridan's lady could do so well as one of his critics

parts.words: Sheridan's lady could do so well as one of his critics
parts.note: Lady ... in The School for Scandal, and a critic of that name in The Critic, both plays by Sheridan

explanation.walkthrough: Lady Sneerwell's name splits into the act and 'well'; Sheridan's The Critic has a character so named.
explanation.definitionFit: To curl the lip in contempt, as Sheridan's scandal-loving lady does well.

clue.text: Feed distributed in hours

indicators.note: distributed letters are scattered and laid out anew in another order

explanation.surface: Meals handed out at intervals through the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges the letters of IN HOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed is to supply with food, sustaining growth.

clue.text: Such a spur for Harry !

parts.note: Harry Percy, the rebel in Shakespeare's Henry IV, was nicknamed Hotspur

explanation.walkthrough: Harry Hotspur (Henry Percy) is the fiery rebel of Shakespeare's Henry IV, Part 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotspur's spur was a fiery, burning one.

clue.text: Not enjoyed during the occupation

parts.note: free time is something one cannot have while at work, an occupation being a job

explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' suggests a wartime military occupation, but it means employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time away from work cannot be had while one is busy at a job.

clue.text: Time defined as free of employment initially

annotationWithheld.why: Time defined as free of employment initially (5): 'Time' is the enemy (old slang 'how goes the enemy?'), but no parse of the rest builds ENEMY from the words held, which the scan confirms
annotationWithheld.clue: Time defined as free of employment initially

clue.text: Society job Ben Gunn might qualify for?

definitions.text: Society job Ben Gunn might qualify for?

parts.words: Society job Ben Gunn might qualify for
parts.note: the castaway in Stevenson's novel had found the buried pirate hoard, so he is one who holds riches

explanation.walkthrough: Ben Gunn, marooned in Treasure Island, had dug up Flint's hoard; the club officer looking after funds is named as though a holder of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A society's officer who keeps the funds, punningly one who has a hoard.
